### Problem

The release candidate v7.19.0 fails the release scenario `bug-by-person-merges` in what the engine did: its `until` or `expect` did not hold, or could no longer hold, so the lane releases nothing and `v7` stays where it is.
Reproduced by: https://github.com/DiluxOne/.github/actions/runs/44677178687 scenario `bug-by-person-merges`.

Cause, verified in the test repository: #887's fix (G7 no longer asks `description_matches` of a pull request of the fixed change alone) works, and the next gate stops it. On DiluxOne/diluxone-test#3147, whose only file is the fixed change `scenarios/bug-by-person-merges/3114.test.md`, the auto-merge decision said "A human merges this one: the review does not find C1 met (G6)": the review's record has C1 `met: false` ("The only test, `3114.test.md`, is a stub with no assertion, so nothing proves the criterion"). The review judged the marker file as a real fix again, this time in its criteria verdict. The fix: in the test repository whose pack says `autopilot: fixed-change`, G6 counts every criterion of a pull request whose only changed files are its fixed change's files as met by construction, as #887 did for the description (one marker per criterion is what the fixed change writes); the review profile says so too. Test: `decide` with a criteria verdict of all false merges such a pull request, and any other file still needs the review's verdict.

### Scope

- The cause of the failure above, in the engine, fixed with a test that would have caught it.

### Out of scope

- Changing the gates or what they check.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given v7.19.0's candidate with the fix, when the release lane plays `bug-by-person-merges` in the test repository, then it passes and the lane releases it.

### Criticality

Critical
